'''Alain Bensoussan''' (born 12 May 1940) is a French mathematician. He is Professor Emeritus at the [[Paris Dauphine University|University of Paris-Dauphine]] and Professor at the [[University of Texas at Dallas|University of Texas]] at [[Dallas]].

== Early life and education ==
Alain Bensoussan was born on 12 May 1940 in [[Tunis, Tunisia]].{{cn|date=October 2025}} Bensoussan is a former student of the [[École Polytechnique|École polytechnique]] (X1960), a graduate of [[ENSAE ParisTech|ENSAE]] and a doctor of mathematics from the Faculty of Sciences in Paris (1969)<ref name=cv>{{cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Bensoussan_Alain/CV|title=Curriculum vitae|publisher=Academia Europaea|access-date=2025-10-13}}</ref> under the supervision of [[Jacques-Louis Lions]].<ref name=mg>{{mathgenealogy|71303}}</ref>

== Career ==
He was a lecturer at the École polytechnique from 1970 to 1986 and a professor at the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École normale supérieure]] from 1980 to 1985.{{cn|date=October 2025}} He was Director of the [[European Institute for Advanced Studies in Management]], Brussels from 1975 to 1977. He was President of [[French Institute for Research in Computer Science and Automation|INRIA]] from 1984 to 1996, President of the [[CNES|National Centre for Space Studies]] (CNES) from 1996 to 2003, President of the Council of the [[European Space Agency]] (ESA) from 1999 to 2002.<ref name=cv/>

His former students include [[Peng Shige]], [[Guy Pujolle]], [[Étienne Pardoux]], [[Jean-Michel Lasry]].<ref name=mg/>

== Awards and honours ==

* Member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Académie des sciences|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-de-l-Academie-des-sciences-/-B/alain-bensoussan.html|publication-date=}}</ref>
* [[Gay-Lussac Humboldt Prize]] (1984)
* [[IEEE]] Fellow (1985)
* Member of [[Academia Europaea]] (1985)
* Commandeur of the [[Ordre national du Mérite|Ordre National du Mérite]] (2000)
* Member of the [[French Academy of Technologies]] (2000)<ref>{{cite web|title=Académie des technologies|url=https://www.academie-technologies.fr/members/11-alain-bensoussan|publication-date=|access-date=2019-09-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190426123310/https://www.academie-technologies.fr/members/11-alain-bensoussan|archive-date=2019-04-26|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* Member of the [[International Academy of Astronautics]] (2001)
* Distinguished Public Service Medal, [[NASA]] (2001)
* Special award from the [[Association Aéronautique et Astronautique de France|Association aéronautique et astronautique de France]] (2002)
* Officier of the Légion d'Honneur (2003)<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sccv.fr/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/AlainBensoussan.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2019-09-11 |archive-date=2019-04-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190426123313/http://www.sccv.fr/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/AlainBensoussan.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* Officer of the Order of Merit of the [[Federal Republic of Germany]] (2003)
* [[SIAM]] Fellow, 2009
* Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (2012)<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |access-date=2019-09-11 |archive-date=2018-08-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* Reid Award (2014)
* Top 2% most highly cited scientists <ref>[https://scholars.cityu.edu.hk/en/prizes/top-2-most-highly-cited-scientists(41901e4d-1569-4a2a-8db5-bfa4c9c1a228).html  Top 2% most highly cited scientists]</ref>
* [[IEEE Control Systems Award]] 2024
